title: Words, Work and Lasting Roots
overview: This chapter is a collection of short sayings that set wise and foolish living side by side, with special attention to how we speak, how we work and who we listen to.

parts.label: Correction and firm roots (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Being willing to be corrected is treated as the doorway to real knowledge, while refusing it is called senseless and dull. Success built on wrongdoing is pictured as shallow, but a good person is like a tree whose roots hold even when the branches shake.

parts.label: Home, plans and reputation (vv. 4-9)
parts.note: Written from a man's point of view in an ancient household, verse 4 says a wife of good character brings honor, while one who brings shame eats away at him like a disease in the bones. The sayings then compare honest and scheming plans and words, and verse 9 says it is better to live modestly with enough than to put on a show while going hungry.

parts.label: Kindness and honest work (vv. 10-12)
parts.note: A good person even pays attention to what their animals need, while a cruel person's idea of kindness still hurts. Steady work on your own land feeds you, but chasing empty schemes does not; verse 12 is hard to translate, and scholars are unsure of its exact meaning.

parts.label: The power of speech (vv. 13-23)
parts.note: Careless or lying words trap the speaker, reckless words wound like a sword, and wise words heal; truth lasts while lies are soon found out. A fool thinks they are always right and reacts to every insult, while a wise person listens, lets slights go and does not blurt out everything they know.

parts.label: Effort, worry and the path of life (vv. 24-28)
parts.note: Hard work leads to independence, while laziness ends in having to work for others, and verse 27 pictures a lazy hunter who will not even cook what he caught. Worry weighs a person down but a kind word lifts them, and the last verse says the right path leads to life; whether it also means life beyond death is debated, since the Hebrew is uncertain.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether sayings like verse 21, which says the righteous are kept from harm, describe how life generally tends to go or are firm promises from God, especially since books like Job show good people suffering.
think: When has a correction or a kind word from someone actually changed something for you, and what made it possible to hear it?
